To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a semi-supervised one-class algorithm for seizure detection that can be adapted to each individual patient using only one night of patient-specific not-annotated data.

(i) a transfer learning method can be used to adapt a patient-independent seizure detection algorithm to patient-specific characteristics, (ii) this leads to a 4-fold decrease of false alarms per night compared to the patient-independence algorithm, (iii) the algorithm has a sensitivity of 88% and a specificity of 99%, (iv) the algorithm requires 1 night of un-annotated data, and (v) the algorithm is able to detect strong nocturnal convulsions.
we developed a patient-specific seizure detection algorithm that can be trained on a single night of patient-specific non-seizure data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a patient-specific seizure detection algorithm that can be used in a home environment.
a novel patient-specific seizure detection algorithm based on transfer learning.
the development of a seizure detection algorithm that is able to adapt to the patient-specific heart rate variability.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method is able to detect seizures with high accuracy and a low false alarm rate.
the proposed method is a promising approach for patient-specific heart rate based seizure prediction.
the method is capable of detecting seizures in a pediatric population, with an accuracy comparable to the state-of-the-art, and with a false alarm rate of less than 1 per night.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the proposed algorithm is able to detect seizures with a low false alarm rate and is able to be adapted to each individual patient with a small amount of patient-specific data.
a patient-specific algorithm can be created in a fast and accurate way with the proposed approach.
the proposed method is a good candidate for a patient-specific algorithm in a home environment.

the patient-specific algorithm is able to detect the seizures with a high sensitivity while keeping the false alarm rate low.

a patient-specific heart rate based seizure detector can be constructed with a very small amount of patient-specific data and that this is a promising direction to improve the performance of seizure detectors.
the proposed method is able to learn from the patient-specific data to improve the performance of the seizure detection algorithm, without the need for a large dataset of seizure and control periods.
